title: Least squares-based biomass conversion and expansion factors best estimate biomass than ratio-based ones: Statistical evidences based on tropical timber species
author: Magalhães, Mate

steps.title: Select sample trees
steps.instruction: In Mozambique (coordinates 18° 15′ S, 35° 00′ E), choose trees from four timber species: Colophytum mopane, Afzelia quanzensis, Millettia stuhlmannii, and Pterocarpus angolensis. Sample a total of 75 trees: 17 C. mopane (harvested in Mabalane district, Gaza province), 24 A. quanzensis, 15 M. stuhlmannii, and 19 P. angolensis (the latter three harvested in Funhalouro district, Inhambane province and Cheringoma district, Sofala province).

steps.title: Measure DBH and fell tree
steps.instruction: Measure the diameter at breast height (DBH) of each selected tree. Fell the tree leaving a predefined stump height of 20 cm.

steps.title: Separate above‑ground components
steps.instruction: Divide the above‑ground portion of the felled tree into four components: stem, branches, foliage, and crown (where crown = branches + foliage).

steps.title: Process stem segments
steps.instruction: For the stem, create five equal‑length segments, measure the diameter at the midpoint of each segment, and calculate segment volume using Hohenadl’s formula. Fresh‑weight each segment in the field. From the top of each segment remove a disc sample for drying.

substeps.instruction: Oven‑dry each disc at 105 °C until constant mass is reached.
Determine the dry‑to‑fresh mass ratio for each disc.
Multiply the ratio by the fresh mass of the corresponding segment to obtain the segment’s dry mass.
Sum the dry masses of all five segments to obtain the total stem dry mass.

steps.title: Process primary branches
steps.instruction: After stripping leaves, fresh‑weight each primary branch together with its secondary and higher‑order branches and twigs. Collect a disc from the primary branch and additional samples of the secondary branches, higher‑order branches, and twigs.

substeps.instruction: Oven‑dry all branch samples at 105 °C until constant mass.
Calculate the dry‑to‑fresh mass ratio from the disc and apply it to the fresh mass of the whole primary branch to obtain its dry mass.

steps.title: Process foliage
steps.instruction: Weigh all foliage from the crown in the field. Collect an approximate 5 % subsample of the fresh foliage mass for drying.

substeps.instruction: Oven‑dry the foliage subsample at 105 °C until constant mass.
Apply the dry‑to‑fresh mass ratio to the total fresh foliage mass to obtain foliage dry mass.
